The speaker sees all businesses as a pipeline: marketing (get strangers to notice you / eyeballs on the brand), then a sales transformation event that turns interest into money, then fulfillment where you deliver what you promised, then an administrative wheel that keeps the machine running.
The same four-stage pipeline applies across different business stacks, including ecom, and the four working in perfect concert is what makes you profit.
Marketing and sales work in tandem, not one or the other, so material built for marketing with Claude Code will also be built for or with the sales department.

The framework used for the Claude Code automations is called RACE, which stands for reach, acquire, close and expand; everything to the left of the delineator is technically marketing and everything to the right is technically sales.

The course focuses on reach (how do I get seen — impressions, views, brand in front of more eyeballs) and acquire (turning impressions and views into intent — booking meetings, form fills, newsletter sign-ups, opt-ins), and all automations developed will focus on reach and acquire.

If you think about business in the RACE framework and race to implement automations that help with reach, acquisition, close and expansion, typically you will allocate your time a lot more effectively than otherwise.

When clients ask for crazy admin or backend automations, the speaker tells them to start with RACE — reach, acquire, close and expand — and worry about the other things later; he finds results are through the roof because people focus on revenue and growth way less than they realistically should.

qualifiers.condition: client asks for admin/backend automation first

raw_claims.text: Under reach there are three major places to build Claude automations, the first being creative: the generation, using artificial intelligence and orchestrated by Claude, of images, videos, audio and so on, typically for advertising and also for organic brand reach and brand growth.

You can significantly reduce bottlenecks at the creative stage by throwing a couple of different creative models to Claude and giving Claude the ability to press buttons and arrange prompts in its own way.

The speaker used the same creative system at a company doing over a billion dollars a year in revenue to massively increase their top of funnel and the total number of pieces of content and ads they get out.

Copy is the second reach lever, in tandem with creative for advertising, and Claude Code can be used to customize copy in the marketing mix, for instance customizing newsletter copy, which the speaker thinks is a big lever not a lot of people are pulling.

Instead of a newsletter saying only what your offer does, you can customize it to reference something the recipient talked about recently, for example on LinkedIn, before presenting the offer; that sort of stuff does really really well and blurs the line with direct outreach.
